issue.title: test_derived_only_collision_returns_composed_template fails under the full parallel lane, passes in isolation
issue.description:
tests/ace/tui/modals/test_snippet_name_modal.py::test_derived_only_collision_returns_composed_template fails intermittently under the whole-suite parallel lane and passes immediately in isolation.

MOST RECENT REPRODUCTION: 2026-08-17T10:55Z, epic phase sase-o8.2 (durable common-placeholder context store). Diff under test was src/sase/history/prompt_placeholders.py plus tests/history/test_prompt_placeholders.py -- no ACE TUI, snippet, or modal code. The scoped lane escalated to the full suite: 31864 passed, 2 failed. This node's failure signature is a stalled modal verdict: after the test's pause(0.25) the modal verdict still read 'Checking ⇥ todo in ...' instead of the expected composed-template result, i.e. the derived-name collision check had not resolved yet. An isolation re-run of the same node passed.

EARLIER INDEPENDENT OBSERVATION: phase sase-lh.2 (2026-08-14) recorded this same node failing in a scoped/full runner alongside another node, noting 'both pass standalone and touch files untouched by this phase' and asking whether the runner needs stronger isolation or resource limits under multi-agent contention.

SIGNATURE: the assertion is a fixed pause(0.25) waiting on an async collision/derivation check. Under a loaded parallel lane 0.25s is not enough for the worker to settle, so this looks like an attempt-unbounded wait rather than cross-test state leakage -- distinguishing it from the process-global-state class. tools/check_test_wait_helpers exists precisely to catch pause-based waits (sase-iy.3 migrated a batch of them); worth checking whether this node's wait is inside that tool's blind spot.

SCOPE: reproduce with 'just test-contention tests/ace/tui/modals/test_snippet_name_modal.py' (and a whole-suite repeat if file-scoped contention stays green, as it did for sase-mv), then either replace the pause(0.25) with a bounded wait-until helper or, if the node proves to be cross-test poisoning instead, root-cause the leak. Decide explicitly whether it belongs in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt if it cannot be fixed by mechanism -- that is how sibling node sase-ke was finally settled.

IMPACT: every agent whose tree reaches the escalated full lane can go red on a node unrelated to its diff, then has to re-run in isolation to prove it.

PROPOSED BY: closed phase bead sase-o8.2 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note), routed here by the sase-o8 land agent. Size large: no root cause is confirmed yet and the pause-vs-leak question has to be measured first.

evidence.note:
Independent reproduction of the SAME defect on a second node in the same module: tests/ace/tui/modals/test_snippet_name_modal.py::test_new_trigger_returns_empty_starting_body. Found by the sase-pv land agent while running `just check-full` on master de06c55ca.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED, not inferred. That node is test_snippet_name_modal.py:108-136, and line 121 is a bare `await pilot.pause(0.25)` immediately followed by asserting `"Create ⇥ todo" in modal.query_one("#snippet-name-verdict", Static).render().plain`. That is the identical fixed-pause-on-an-async-verdict shape this bead already describes for test_derived_only_collision_returns_composed_template: under a loaded lane 0.25s is not enough for the collision/derivation worker to settle, so the verdict is still "Checking ⇥ todo in ..." when the assertion reads it. One remediation -- replace the fixed pause with a bounded wait on the settled verdict -- fixes both nodes, so this is the same root cause, not merely the same file.

EVIDENCE, 4 full-run failures after the baseline's 2026-08-15T17:22:27Z cutoff, across two workspaces and four distinct heads:
  20260816T055210Z  head 3a783a411  ws sase_17  tree dirty  (130 failures in run)
  20260817T011647Z  head 4819a0314  ws sase_17  tree dirty  (2 failures in run)
  20260818T033312Z  head c033ca4c4  ws sase_12  tree dirty  (10 failures in run)
  20260818T234410Z  head 11f78656d  ws sase_12  TREE CLEAN  (sole failure in the run)
The last record is the strongest: a clean tree where this node was the only failure in the entire full lane, so it is not collateral of someone's in-progress edit.

NOT REPRODUCED serially: 3/3 passes on master de06c55ca with `-p no:randomly`, 1.4s each. Parallel-lane only, same as this bead's existing signature.

IMPACT, which is new: this node has now crossed the flake-baseline gate's bar. `just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake` -- the last step of `just check-full` -- is red on it, so it blocks landings rather than merely annoying runs. I am adding a baseline entry naming this bead as owner for both nodes per tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt's header; the entries are debt for whoever fixes the wait.
